    Sidecar multi-dimensional index evaluation and security probe design for cloud native environment

    View summary
    Wenrui Xie and Xin Gu
    ISBN9798400721113
    Pages461 - 465
    Abstract

    With a large number of traditional applications migrating to the cloud in the form of microservices, cloud service providers frequently encounter various functional service exceptions or interruptions, which is basically attributable to the fact that when the basic K8s container applications are automatically started or destroyed, a large number of functional dependencies generate or cause abnormal errors that cause program failures, which requires scientific methods to analyze the causes. This paper takes the auxiliary container Sidecar as the research object. First, it analyzes the reasons why it cannot monitor the operation of the main container and the failure and collapse of the main container, and proposes a Sidecar security monitoring index system. Then, according to the index system, it develops a Sidecar security monitoring probe to ensure the normal operation of K8s cluster content servers and the security and reliability of cloud services.

Abstract
With a large number of traditional applications migrating to the
cloud in the form of microservices, cloud service providers fre-
quently encounter various functional service exceptions or inter-
ruptions, which is basically attributable to the fact that when the
basic K8s container applications are automatically started or de-
stroyed, a large number of functional dependencies generate or
cause abnormal errors that cause program failures, which requires
scientific methods to analyze the causes. This paper takes the aux-
iliary container Sidecar as the research object. First, it analyzes the
reasons why it cannot monitor the operation of the main container
and the failure and collapse of the main container, and proposes a
Sidecar security monitoring index system. Then, according to the
index system, it develops a Sidecar security monitoring probe to
ensure the normal operation of K8s cluster content servers and the
security and reliability of cloud services.

1 Introductionn
In recent years, the country has been vigorously promoting the
digital transformation of enterprises[1], and the use of cloud has be-
come the general trend of traditional enterprises. The development
of technologies such as cloud native, microservices, and container-
ization plays an irreplaceable role in digital transformation. The
sidecar[2] is a container running with the main container. The
two containers share resources such as pod memory and network
interface, and provide functions such as load balancing and traffic
management. The separation of microservices in the cloud envi-
ronment is becoming more and more complex, and it is difficult to
sort out the calls between thousands of microservices. The frequent
occurrence of various types of functional service exceptions or in-
terruptions by cloud service vendors is basically attributed to the
fact that when the K8S container-based application is automatically
started or destroyed, a large number of functional dependencies
generate or cause abnormal errors to cause service failure. The
side car container cannot identify the unavailable main container,
causing the key link of the cloud service to be interrupted, result-
ing in a large area of exceptions or system crashes[3], resulting in
unsustainable cloud services.
In the container application, there are many researches on the
main container flow and safety monitoring at the present stage,
and less attention is paid to the test ability of the sidecar itself, such
as the permission and service availability of the sidecar. Whether
the sidecar service is available and the safety is credible cannot be
accurately measured, and the sidecar test evaluation index system
is lacking. When the sidecar encounters an attack or cannot start
normally, the main container traffic and other business conditions
cannot be observed. Once a problem occurs, it cannot be grasped
in time, resulting in abnormal or interrupted services of various
functions of the cloud service. Therefore, based on the safety and
observable characteristics of containers, this paper proposes a mon-
itoring and evaluation method for sidecar from the perspective of
microservice governance[4], develops sidecar monitoring probes,
builds safety assessment infrastructure, and guides cloud service
providers to establish and improve container monitoring and safety
capabilities. The rest of this paper is structured as follows: Section461

2 Container monitoring method and sidecar
failure cause analysis
2.1 Container monitoring method
Container monitoring is the process of tracking application perfor-
mance by collecting and analyzing performance metrics. Due to
its transient nature, containers are quite complex and more chal-
lenging to monitor compared to traditional applications running
on virtual or bare-metal servers. The container is short and state-
less, and needs to collect indicators and logs and immediately send
them to a centralized location for storage. Otherwise, once the
container is deleted, the log will also be deleted. Therefore, each
main container is usually equipped with a sidecar container to
achieve additional monitoring and auxiliary functions, such as log
collection, traffic control, and data caching[5].
The mainstream cloud-native manufacturers in the industry, in
addition to using sidecar containers for business container mon-
itoring, also utilize open-source professional software such as
Prometheus[6] and Loki[7] to monitor cloud-native containers. This
is because there are many business scenarios, complex relationships
between containers, and multi-layer connections, requiring overall
monitoring and planning of the entire cloud-native business.
2.2 Analysis of the causes of sidecar failure
Analyzing the causes of sidecar failure is crucial for the development
of cloud services and helps to solve practical problems encountered
by enterprises in their adoption and usage of cloud services. Based
on cases and practical experiences of Sidecar failures, this section
summarizes the major reasons for Sidecar failures and provides the-
oretical support for the monitoring model and solutions proposed
in the next chapter.
Sidecar failure problems are mostly related to pod life cycle
management defects[8]. If a pod has multiple containers, it will
normally start or destroy at the same time, but in some scenar-
ios, the dependence on the order of container start or destruction
will cause problems. The first is to start order dependence. The
startup sequence of the main container and the Sidecar lacks a
coordination mechanism. When the business container starts, it
needs to call other services. Due to the delay of the sidecar startup,
the service invocation fails, which in turn triggers the pod startup
cycle. The second is to terminate the order conflict. In the process
of destroying pod, k8s will send SIGTERM signal to all containers
at the same time, and the main container will compete with Sidecar
for destruction. The main container needs to call external services
during the shutdown process, and sidecar has stopped receiving
new requests, resulting in task interruption and destruction failure.
Resource competition between containers and sidecar permis-
sion configuration is too high. Sidecars share resources with the
primary container, which poses a risk in resource-constrained en-
vironments where traffic surges can easily lead to out of memory
errors or cpu spikes, thereby causing service interruptions. Fur-
thermore, when a sidecar is configured with overly permissive
permissions, such as the ability to mount sensitive directories, it
can be exploited for container escape or lateral penetration. This
not only disrupts service but also introduces serious security vul-
nerabilities.
Supply chain attacks and vulnerability introduction. Malicious
attackers can trick developers into installing malicious sidecars
through supply chain attacks. Once an attacker visits the sidecar,
any misconfiguration or loose security mechanisms can put the
entire cluster at risk. When there is a container with a security
vulnerability, even if the container does not open network access,
an attacker can still connect to the management interface through
the container network to obtain the permissions of the container
host. As shown in Figure 1, a small vulnerability may break through
the container node[9].If there is a container escape vulnerability
in docker, container, etc., an attacker can use this vulnerability
to obtain the control of the host and maliciously call the relevant
container.
3 Sidecar monitoring model and security probe
3.1 Construction of sidecar safety monitoring
index system
While bringing decoupling and convenience, Sidecar also intro-
duces new attack surfaces and potential vulnerabilities, including
CVE mirroring vulnerabilities, configuration errors, dependency
vulnerabilities, IPC vulnerabilities and other security issues. In the
network attack surface, sidecar has problems such as port exposure
and network strategy bypass; in the host attack surface, sidecar
faces malicious code attacks and privilege escalation; in the run-
time attack surface, sidecar encounters malicious process injection.
Therefore, based on the causes of sidecar failures discussed in sec-
tion 2 and combined with the security issues of sidecar, this section
proposes a sidecar security monitoring indicator system to provide
security protection for sidecar, reduce risks to an acceptable level,
and support the safe operation of large-scale microservices.The
sidecar security monitoring indicator system is shown in Table 1,
including indicator composition, thresholds, and related Notes.
Basic monitoring index layer: The basic test indicators of this
layer include two secondary indicators: resource indicators and
health status. CPU usage refers to the cpu occupancy rate of the
sidecar container at runtime, to avoid the sidecar occupying too
much resources and causing the container to collapse; the memory
occupies the memory usage of the sidecar container; the port num-
ber indicates that the side car container listens to the network port
number of the main container to prevent network conflicts caused
by listening to the same port; the disk read and write rate of the
disk I/O sidecar container; traffic hijacking refers to whether the
vehicle container correctly intercepts/forwards the traffic of the
main container.
Health status: the start-up order refers to the container start-up
sequence and dependency relationship, monitoring the failure of
the sidecar to invoke the service due to the start-up dependency; the
destruction order refers to the container termination order, moni-
toring the problem that the sidecar cannot be destroyed; sidecar log
refers to collecting the running log of the sidecar and monitoring462

Container permission refers to monitoring whether sidecar en-
ables privileged container permissions and controls it to have the
principle of minimizing permissions; secure mirroring refers to
monitoring whether the mirror image of the sidecar passes signa-
ture verification to ensure that the mirror source is credible; identity
authentication refers to the dynamic verification of the identity of
the sidecar to prevent counterfeiting attacks; sensitive path refers
to monitoring whether the sidecar is loaded with sensitive infor-
mation or directories to prevent data leakage; behavior monitoring
refers to monitoring the daily behavior of the sidecar to prevent
unexpected file reading and other behaviors.
By constructing the above-mentioned edge container security
monitoring index system, it is beneficial to achieve a comprehen-
sive understanding of the behavior and safety of edge containers,
enhance the governance capability of cloud service meshes, and
provide a theoretical foundation for edge container testing.
3.2 Sidecar safety monitoring probe
Based on the research of sidecar monitoring indicator system in
Section 3.1, a detection probe tool for Sidecar monitoring (refer
to SidecarMon) was developed to ensure the safe monitoring of
sidecar and guarantee the normal operation of business. Sidecar-
Mon adopts a ”dual plane and three-layer” architecture, separating
the control plane from the data plane, achieving both lightweight
and real-time capabilities; it monitors non-intrusively, avoiding
direct modification of business code. When abnormalities in side-
car are detected, the probe can take measures to block them and
generate alerts and other information. The main architecture and
implementation of SidecarMon are shown in Figure 2.
As shown in Figure 2, sidecar security monitoring probe is com-
posed of three layers: control plane, data plane and alarm response463

layer. The core components of the control plane include the strat-
egy management center, the pre-set detection range and detection
method, and the fault handling method. The strategy management
center is a collection of a series of dynamically issued detection
policies, such as CVE vulnerability feature library, permission col-
lection, etc; Pre-set detection range and detection method, that is
customize the monitoring sidecar range, detection frequency, fail-
ure window duration, etc., to avoid misjudgment caused by single
jitter. Fault handling means that when sidecar failure is detected,
different handling methods are implemented according to different
failure causes. If security attacks cause sidecar failure or abnormal
operations, security tools will be called for processing.
The data plane monitors the data and information related to
sidecar. The core components include the probe acquisition layer
and the local rule engine. The eBPF in the probe acquisition layer
captures key events such as sidecar network traffic and process
behavior through the eBPF program; The container runtime inter-
face obtains sidecar metadata, such as resource utilization, through
the Container Runtime Interface (CRI) to provide data support for
the control plane; API hooking monitors configuration changes by
hijacking the service grid management interface to ensure that the
main container and sidecar can communicate normally. The local
rule engine performs real-time filtering based on predefined rules
such as Falco rule syntax for preliminary threat determination, as
shown in Table 2. Data masking is to mask sensitive information;
Threshold alarm refers to the alarm triggered when the index ex-
ceeds the reasonable threshold of the user-defined Sidecar, such as
the risk of resource exhaustion.
The alarm response layer is composed of alarm rules and re-
sponse actions. It is the execution layer of the sidecar security
monitoring probe tool and interacts with the data plane in real time.
The alarm rule sets a series of sidecar failure risk indicators, such as
the memory footprint of the resource class is greater than 80%, the
security class finds abnormal processes, Sidecar permissions are
too high, and the coverage of sidecar running abnormal indicators
is realized. The response action is the response of SidecarMon to
the failure of sidecar when the alarm rule occurs as shown in Table
3, including a series of actions such as restarting sidecar, clearing
sidecar ’s hijacking traffic rules, reducing sidecar’s permissions,
and fixing vulnerabilities to ensure the sidecar container’s normal
start-stop and operation.
As Prometheus,we package the sidecarMon into a container mir-
ror and directly pull it to the K8s cluster environment when the
host machine starts. Create a Deployment to define the sidecarMon
container and its configuration, and add a startup command in
the mirror launcher to start the probe, in order to complete the
deployment of sidecarMon on microservice business. SidecarMon
retrieves sidecar data from remote machines via HTTP or docker
Daemon API and stores it in a local temporal database. The prin-
ciple of sidecarMon implementation is bytecode injection, which
converts the class files that need to be injected into a byte array
and injects them into the running program through a pre-set inter-
ceptor. As Prometheus, sidecarMon does not require modifying the
source code of the business system, is deployed independently, pro-
cesses independently, and does not invade the business to achieve
distributed monitoring, with strong scalability. The resource and464

4 Conclusion
This paper takes the main container auxiliary container sidecar
in the cloud native service as the research object, and studies its
testing and security monitoring capabilities. Firstly, the causes
of sidecar failure and collapse are analyzed, and then the sidecar
safety monitoring index system is proposed based on the reasons.
Finally, the sidecar safety monitoring probe is developed based on
the safety monitoring index system, and the tool architecture and
functions are designed. The SidecarMon is expected to be completed
in the near future.The sidecar security monitoring index system
and SidecarMon can be extended to all sidecars in the k8s cluster
in the cloud native environment. In the future, with the popularity
of the zero-trust architecture, SidecarMon will further integrate
identity authentication and dynamic strategies to become the core
component of cloud-native security.
